chapter: Fletcher, Wooding and the Harlem scene
title: The 1920s big band business
summary: After 1922 big bands were everywhere in ballrooms like Roseland, a billion-dollar business before radio and television.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Was there quite a few bands at that time?
Oh, big bands, yes. All bands were big. Ten and more. That was during the big band era, all the 20's From the first -- after '22 the big bands started. Whiteman started the big band idea.
They were all pretty active, I mean there was --

Oh, yes, they all worked. They all worked. They made records or they worked on spots or big ballrooms. New York had -- well, the Roseland hired two big bands and the Rosemont in Brooklyn, the one at 53rd and Broadway hired two big bands. They were touring the country giving dances. The band business was just a billion dollar concern.
All that was before television and radio.
Before television and radio -- radio was coming on then, but television was unthought of. Nobody had dreamed of television.
